assumptions.obligation: i_rst_n is held at 0 from time zero for at least 2 clock cycles. The first cycle is already assumed, so only the second cycle is added.

When AWVALID was 1 with AWREADY at 0 and reset was not asserted in either cycle, AWVALID stays 1 and AWADDR/AWPROT stay stable until the AW transfer. Reset ends the obligation, and a valid after R1 is a new request.
When WVALID was 1 with WREADY at 0 and reset was not asserted in either cycle, WVALID stays 1 and WDATA/WSTRB stay stable until the W transfer. Reset ends the obligation.
When ARVALID was 1 with ARREADY at 0 and reset was not asserted in either cycle, ARVALID stays 1 and ARADDR/ARPROT stay stable until the AR transfer. Reset ends the obligation.

notes:
The constraints are 4 assumptions plus one counter, r_init_cnt. The counter sets the length of reset at start-up and tells when $past values can be used.

**Two choices for the reviewer at gate G3:**
- **Payload checked for stability (ENV-02, ENV-04):** awprot and arprot are included, because the AXI payload includes them (RF-12.1-01). The block ignores these signals (RF-1.3-02). If the reviewer wants to see prot change while a valid is waiting, the prot stability lines can be removed safely.
- **"No transfer" condition:** it uses only `valid && !ready` in the previous cycle, with i_rst_n at 1 then and now. If reset is asserted, the obligation ends (RF-12.1-10). The cycle after R1 is not constrained, so a valid there is a new request (RF-12.1-11).

**Left free on purpose:**
- **bready and rready:** the manager may hold them at 0, set them early, or make them depend on the valid (RF-12.1-02).
- **i_status:** it can take any value. In the sampled model it already only changes between edges (RF-12.1-05).
- **Valids during reset:** any value is allowed (RF-12.1-07).
- **Reset after start-up:** it can be asserted again at any time.
- **Addresses, strobes and prot values:** all are allowed, including unaligned addresses and strobe 4'b0000.

**Not expressible here:**
- **Recovery and removal timing of the reset release (RF-12.1-03):** this is a timing requirement and can't be written as an assumption in a cycle-based model.
- **No X or Z values (RF-12.1-06):** formal tools already use only 0 and 1, so no assumption is needed.
